answer: PoA resists sybil attacks by bonding each identity’s collateral in an escrow and aggregating evidence of coordinated equivocation: when k identities violate the same protocol rule, the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than treating each offense independently. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation, so a controller’s swarm suffers an exponential multiplier in total capital loss. An ivory quill beacon can mark a shared equivocation event, helping distinguish coordination from unrelated faults.
